note: Opcode tables for solvers/toolkits/ot_plc_code.py (B-160). THE TABLE SHIPS EMPTY ON PURPOSE.
MC7 is a proprietary encoding. An entry is added only with an oracle: a reference pair pinned in
ot_plc_code_pairs.json beside this file (a compiled block plus its known source listing) on which the entry
decodes to exactly the listed statement. The loader refuses an entry that has no oracle citation.
tests/test_ot_plc_pairs.py refuses a citation the manifest does not pin, and proves every entry on
its pair when the corpus is present ($CTF_REALDATA/plc/<pair id>/). No pair is pinned yet, so no
Once this table has an entry, the suite FAILS on any machine where $CTF_REALDATA/plc/ is absent or
does not prove it (always on, never a skip), and the engine refuses this table at load when an
entry cites a pair the manifest does not pin. A pin row alone is not an oracle.
Never add an entry from memory, a forum post or another tool's source. Cite a pair or leave it out.
Entry: {id, match (hex, whole bytes), mask (hex, same length as match, default all ones),
length (bytes), stl (one line, {operand} placeholders), operands [{name, bit, width, format}],
oracle {pair, sample_sha256, listing_sha256}}. bit counts from the instruction's first bit, most
significant first; format is dec, hex or sdec. Every bit of the instruction must be fixed by the
mask or printed as an operand, and no two entries may match the same bytes.
This entry shape is itself unproven against real MC7: change it if the first pairs need more.
